notes: PROMOTED 2026-09-18. This entry is the second half of a two-step fold. PR #2712 had already merged fifteen of the seventeen functions into src/game/actors/daPiano_c/d_a_piano.cpp -- the four class methods from their _ZN8MadPiano*.cpp sources and ten helpers from src/unnamed/ov063/ -- but left the destructor pair split in one-line sources, because with the destructor merely declared in the header nothing in the TU defined the key function and the tree had no manifest here to license what the alternative emits. This entry supplies that manifest and folds the pair in, so config/arm9/overlays/ov063/delinks.txt now licenses the whole run 0x0211d4b8..0x0211e1c0 to one file.

THE ONLY CODEGEN-VISIBLE EDIT IS ONE LINE OF HEADER. include/daPiano_c.h changed `virtual ~daPiano_c();` to `virtual ~daPiano_c() {}`. MEASURED 2026-09-18 under the pinned 2004/b56: the inline form emits _ZN9daPiano_cD1Ev then _ZN9daPiano_cD0Ev, with no homeless D2, into the two .text sections immediately ahead of every function written in the file -- so all seventeen sections come out in exactly the cartridge's ascending order, 0x0211d4b8 first and daPiano_c_classInit last. Both bodies byte-MATCH at their cartridge addresses (tools/match.py, --strict-relocs). The cartridge puts D1 below D0 here, which is the order the inline form produces, so this class needed none of the destructor-order machinery: no pragma, no forcing scaffold, no partial boundary. The earlier out-of-line experiment recorded in notes/experiments/piano-2712-dtor-split.md is not contradicted -- it measured writing the destructor body into the .cpp, which makes the TU the key-function home and emits a D2 the licensed run cannot carry.

The eleven compiler_only_output rows are what the inline destructor costs. With a definition of the destructor visible, this TU becomes a candidate emitter for the class's vague-linkage RTTI, so it emits _ZTV9daPiano_c plus the _ZTI/_ZTS pair for daPiano_c and for each of its four inherited bases. Every one of the eleven has a real cartridge home outside this entry's claimed .text range, so all eleven are deadstrip-data and none is a plain deadstrip. The eight base-class rows carry the same canonical addresses this overlay's other promoted entry, ov063/daObjTh_Fall_Block_c, already verified; each was re-checked against config/arm9/symbols.txt and config/arm9/overlays/ov002/symbols.txt for this entry rather than copied on trust.

daPiano_c_classInit is the one function here whose legacy_source is this entry's own source path, and that is not a copy-paste slip: on this history the factory has never had a per-function file. src/game/actors/daPiano_c/d_a_piano.cpp was created already holding it, and the promotion deletes no file on its account. The two destructor sources ARE deleted by this promotion; the other fourteen legacy_source paths were deleted by PR #2712 and are kept here as the historical record the conventions ask for.

The factory stays hand-rolled. Promotion gives this class a manifest that could now license what `return new daPiano_c()` instantiates on top of the factory's own matching bytes -- dBgActor_c's D2 helper and a re-emitted Vector3 inline destructor -- so the packaging wall the source comment used to name is gone. Converting it is still a codegen change, and promotion changes no codegen; it is left for a follow-up that carries its own byte proof.
